The team project is the capstone of the course — and the only piece of fully
open-ended work. In teams of **3–4**, you'll propose and build an ambitious,
real-world project of your own design, applying every workflow skill from the
semester: version control, planning, skills, verification, continuous integration,
deployment, LLM APIs, MCP, and (where it helps) multi-agent orchestration.

Teams form in Meeting 5. From Meeting 9 on, the last ~45 minutes of each class is
**team studio time**, where the instructor checks in with each team. The final two
meetings are dedicated studio sessions, and we learn collaboration workflows (pull
request reviews, issues, and parallel agents in git worktrees) live in Meeting 12.

**Summary of deliverables:**

Item | Weight | Due
-----|--------|-----------------
[Proposal](1-proposal.qmd) | 5% | Oct 13 (Meeting 8)
[Interim Report](2-interim-report.qmd) | 10% | Nov 10 (Meeting 12)
[Final Report](3-final-report.qmd) | 15% | Dec 1 (Meeting 14)
[Final Presentation](4-presentation.qmd) | 10% | Final exam slot (date TBD)
